q.t: Heat always flows from…
o: A hotter object to a colder one
A colder object to a hotter one
q.e: Heat moves from the hotter part to the colder part, until they are equally warm.

q.t: Heat moving along a metal spoon in hot tea is…
q.e: In solids, each particle passes heat to its neighbour without moving — conduction.

q.t: Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth by…
q.e: Space is empty — there's no medium. Only radiation can carry heat without one.

q.t: Heating water in a pot spreads heat through the water mainly by…
q.e: Hot water rises and cool water sinks, carrying heat round — convection.

q.t: Which is a good conductor of heat?
q.e: Metals like copper conduct heat well, which is why pans are made of metal.

q.t: During the day, the breeze blowing from sea to land is the…
q.e: A breeze is named by where it comes from. In the day it blows from the sea.

q.t: Water turning into vapour when heated by the Sun is…
q.e: Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapour.

q.t: Water vapour cooling to form clouds is…
q.e: Cooling makes vapour condense into tiny droplets, forming clouds.

q.t: Rain, snow and hail falling from clouds is called…
q.e: Precipitation is any water falling from clouds back to the Earth.

q.t: Which colour clothes keep you cooler in summer?
q.e: Light colours reflect most of the heat falling on them; dark ones absorb it.

q.t: In the pin experiment, which pin falls first?
q.e: Heat travels gradually along the strip, so the wax nearest the flame melts first.

q.t: What do the pins falling one by one prove?
o: Heat moves gradually through the material
q.e: If heat appeared everywhere at once, all would fall together. Falling in order shows heat travelling.

q.t: In conduction, the particles of the solid…
o: Stay in place and pass heat on
Move from hot to cold end
q.e: Only the heat travels, passed neighbour to neighbour — the particles don't leave their positions.

q.t: In convection, heat moves by…
o: The movement of the heated particles themselves
q.e: Hot liquid or gas actually moves, carrying heat with it.

q.t: Why does hot air rise?
q.e: Heated air expands, takes up more space and becomes lighter, so it rises; cooler, heavier air sinks.

q.t: Why do woollen clothes keep us warm?
o: They trap air, a poor conductor
q.e: Air trapped in the wool's pores stops body heat escaping.

q.t: Why does tea stay hot longer in a clay cup than a steel cup?
q.e: Clay doesn't let heat out easily; steel conducts it away quickly.

q.t: Which heats up faster in the Sun?
q.e: Soil heats faster than water — and cools faster too. That's what drives land and sea breezes.

q.t: At night, the breeze blows from land to sea. It is called…
q.e: Named by where it comes from: from the land.

q.t: Water evaporating from the leaves of plants is…
q.e: Transpiration is evaporation of water from plants, another source of water vapour.

q.t: Why are two thin blankets warmer than one thick blanket?
q.e: The air layer between the blankets is an extra poor conductor, blocking heat loss.

q.t: Why do coastal houses face their windows towards the sea?
o: To catch the cool sea breeze in the day
q.e: During the day cool air flows from the sea to the land.

q.t: Explain the sea breeze. During the day…
o: Land heats faster, warm air above it rises, cool sea air moves in
Sea heats faster and its air rises
q.e: The warmer land heats the air above it; it rises and cooler air from over the sea flows in.

q.t: In the potassium permanganate experiment, coloured water…
o: Rises in the middle, comes down the sides
q.e: Water heated at the bottom-centre rises; cooler water at the sides sinks to replace it — a convection loop.

q.t: You sit near a campfire and feel warm on your face. This heat reaches you by…
q.e: Heat travels directly from the fire to you, without needing the air to carry it.

q.t: A pan of water on a flame: flame → pan is ___, through the water is ___.
q.e: Heat passes through the solid pan by conduction, then spreads through the water as it moves — convection.

q.t: Why do hollow bricks keep homes comfortable?
o: Trapped air inside is a poor conductor
q.e: Air inside the bricks slows heat flow in both directions — warm in winter, cool in summer.

q.t: A partially inflated balloon left in the Sun grows bigger. Why?
q.e: Heated air takes up more space, so it pushes the balloon out.

q.t: Why does a hot cup of milk cool even if nothing touches it?
q.e: Every object radiates heat; a hot one gives out more than it gets, so it cools.

q.t: Why do wet clothes dry faster on a sunny day?
o: The Sun's heat speeds up evaporation
q.e: More heat means water evaporates faster from the clothes.

q.t: Why does the breeze reverse between day and night at the coast?
o: Land heats and cools faster than sea
The sea gets hotter in the day
q.e: By day land is warmer so air rises there (sea breeze); by night land is cooler so air rises over the sea (land breeze).

q.t: Which process can work in empty space?
q.e: Conduction and convection need particles. Radiation needs no medium.

q.t: The bukhari stove warms a room and cooks food. It uses…
q.e: The iron body conducts, warm air circulates by convection, and heat radiates to people nearby.

q.t: Why are houses in Mori block (Uttarakhand) built with two wooden layers filled with mud and dung?
o: Wood and mud are poor conductors, keeping heat in
q.e: Poor conductors stop heat escaping in the cold mountains.

q.t: Smoke from an incense stick rises because…
o: It is warmer than the surrounding air
It is pulled by the ceiling
q.e: Smoke is hot gas plus tiny particles — warmer and lighter than the surrounding air, so convection carries it up.

q.t: In the pin experiment, a wooden strip is used instead. What happens?
q.e: Wood is a poor conductor, so heat doesn't reach the wax to melt it.

q.t: Which statement about the water cycle is TRUE?
o: It conserves the total water on Earth
q.e: The cycle moves and replenishes water but the total amount stays the same.

q.t: Where does well and handpump water come from?
o: Rainwater that seeps into the ground
q.e: Precipitation soaks into the ground and is stored as groundwater.

q.t: Who gave methods for predicting seasonal rainfall in Brihatsamhita?
q.e: Varahamihira of Ujjaini (6th century CE) used clouds, winds and the positions of stars and the Moon.

q.t: You want to keep ice from melting for long on a picnic. Which box is best?
o: A box with thick walls containing trapped air
A black box in the sun
q.e: Trapped air is a poor conductor and slows heat flowing in. Steel conducts heat in; black absorbs heat.
